summary_md: **fly51fly ([@fly51fly](https://x.com/fly51fly/status/2115913178542719196))** shares UC Berkeley's **Evolving Agent Teams** ([arXiv 2610.36848](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36848)), in which a supervisor restructures a team of agents from execution feedback and a persistent file system; on GPU kernel optimization its MLA decode kernel trajectory ends at roughly 1.2× the production FlashInfer baseline, per the paper's Figure 1.
relevance: Self-reorganizing multi-agent teams for hard engineering problems.

Therapid progress of software engineering agents drives interest in applying them
to open-ended problems such as GPU kernel optimization.However,we find that
existing coding agents converge tolocal optima on real-world, expert-writtenker-
nels (e.g., FLASHINFER).We introduce EVOLVING AGENT TEAMS, a multi-agent
framework that escapes such local optima.Itfeatures (1)a central supervisor
that diagnoses eachlocal optimumand restructures ateam of agents; and(2)a
persistent file system that comprises a learning document, an evolution history,and
per-team artifacts,grounding restructuringwith accumulated experience.Under
